<p dir="auto">
This project 
<a href="https://typer.tiangolo.com/alternatives/#click" rel="nofollow">appears to be</a>
 built on top of and in relation to click, with more modern python type hints at the core of the interface. Additionally, the existing documentation 
<a href="https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/parameter-types/custom-types/#click-custom-type" rel="nofollow">link</a>
s 
<a href="https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/arguments/help/#help-text-for-cli-arguments-in-click" rel="nofollow">to</a>
 click to explain typer's behavior.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
For these reasons, I think think it might be appropriate to set the documentation bar for typer at click's height. Click has 
<a href="https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/8.1.x/#api-reference" rel="nofollow">a full API reference documentation</a>
.
</p>
<p dir="auto">I agree with other commenters here that the documentation would be much appreciated and useful. I think it will be necessary for me be able to convince my coworkers to use typer instead of click for our next python CLI.</p>
